cards.title: Lower Back Spasm Recovery - Myofascial Release
minimal_notes: Daily 10 min protocol.
Use a 2:1 time ratio: spend double time on the tight side.
Expected improvement: 30–40% in 1–2 weeks.
Stop for sharp shooting pain, leg numbness, or bruising.

exercises.name: Psoas lacrosse-ball release
exercises.notes: Face down; ball between hip bone and belly button.

exercises.name: TFL / IT-band lacrosse-ball release
exercises.notes: Side-lying; ball on outer hip.

exercises.name: Rectus femoris release
exercises.notes: Face down; release upper front thigh.

exercises.name: Piriformis lacrosse-ball release
exercises.notes: Sit on ball in figure-4; find tender spot.

exercises.name: Glute med / max lacrosse-ball release
exercises.notes: Side-lying with ball under glute.

exercises.name: QL / lower-back lacrosse-ball release
exercises.notes: Place ball between spine and side of torso; not on spine.

cards.title: Hip Flexor Release Protocol (Pre-Glute Work)
minimal_notes: Start 1 week post-injury, before glute activation protocol.
Frequency: daily, 8–10 min.
Goal: release hip-flexor tightness that inhibits glute activation.
Pick 2 stretches per day; sustainable > perfect.
Do before glute activation work.

exercises.name: Couch stretch
exercises.notes: Back knee on pad; shin vertical against wall/couch; front knee 90°; push hips forward; torso upright.

exercises.name: 90/90 hip stretch
exercises.notes: Front leg externally rotated; back leg internally rotated; sit tall and lean forward over front leg.

exercises.name: Pigeon pose
exercises.notes: Front leg bent, back leg extended; keep hips square; fold forward.

exercises.name: Psoas release with kettlebell
exercises.notes: Lie on back; 12kg KB on hip flexor; pull same-side knee to chest; deep release, not sharp pain.

rotation: Alternative: pick whichever 2 feel best that day.

cards.title: Glute Activation & Strength Protocol (Motor Control Fix)
minimal_notes: Start 1–2 weeks post-injury, after hip-flexor work starts.
Frequency: daily, 10–12 min.
Goal: make glute dominance automatic and prevent lumbar compensation.
This is motor control, not strength training; perfect form always.
If back takes over, stop, rest, restart.
Video reference from note: https://youtu.be/qu1pqo-dbXM?si=ZJlPpYIWZpL9Rd6h at 6:48

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridges
exercises.notes: Pause 3s at top; feel glutes, not hamstrings/back; hand on glute to verify activation; optional other foot resting on working-leg knee.

exercises.name: Clamshells with resistance band
exercises.notes: Slow and controlled; external rotation from glutes; 30s rest between sets.

exercises.name: Intentional kettlebell swings
exercises.notes: Conscious glute snap; not just hip hinge; feel glutes working between sets.

exercises.name: Heavy hip thrusts
exercises.notes: Phase 2 option; tempo 1s up, 2s hold, 2s down.

exercises.name: Light Romanian deadlifts
exercises.notes: Phase 2 option; 4s eccentric; hand on glutes to feel loading.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
exercises.dose: 3 x 6 each leg, bodyweight or 12kg KB
exercises.notes: Phase 2 option.

exercises.name: Fatigue test
exercises.notes: 3 sets hip thrusts near failure, then tempo deadlifts at 60% max / 50kg; pass if pattern holds.

exercises.name: Distraction test
exercises.notes: Deadlift at 60% while someone talks or while doing mental math; pattern must survive divided attention.

attention_split_training: Weeks 2–4: bridges while counting backwards by 7s from 100.
Weeks 2–4: swings while having a conversation or listening to a podcast.

Programming: 2–3x/week on non-consecutive days.
Can pair with upper-body days or use as warm-up before pistols.
Focus on control and feeling target muscles.

cards.title: 🏋️ Convict Conditioning - Big Six Progressions
minimal_notes: Progressive calisthenics program with six fundamental movement patterns and 10 levels each.
Daily routine: 10–15 min, 3-day A/B/C rotation.
Rest 60–90s between sets; cut to 2 sets per exercise for 8–10 min total.
Progress when goal reps feel comfortable for 2 workouts.

exercises.name: Day A — Push & Core Focus
exercises.notes: Push-ups 2–3 sets; leg raises 2–3 sets; handstand practice 1–2 sets; bridges 1–2 sets.

exercises.name: Day B — Legs & Pull Focus
exercises.notes: Squats 2–3 sets; pull-ups 2–3 sets; leg raises 2 sets; bridges light set 1 set.

exercises.name: Day C — Balance & Skill Focus
exercises.notes: Handstand practice 2–3 sets; push-ups 2 sets; squats 2 sets; pull-ups 2 sets.
